items.title: Nothing unveils Ear (note) earbuds with AI note-taking
items.summary: Nothing has unveiled Ear (note), a pair of true wireless earbuds that transcribe and summarize in-person conversations, phone calls and online meetings using on-device AI. The aluminum case adds dedicated Talk and Record buttons inspired by Walkman controls, and the company says the tool will not compromise its best in-ear audio or Hi-Res sound. Pricing and the official launch are set for December 8.

items.title: Onkyo second Dr. STONE earbud collection adds 13 voice lines per model
items.summary: Onkyo announced its second Dr. STONE wireless earbud collaboration on November 26, with the Dr. Xeno, Stanley Snyder and SAI models each carrying 13 newly recorded voice prompts. Based on the CP-TWS01E true wireless platform, all three support active noise cancellation and ambient sound mode, with USB-C and wireless charging for the case. Japan preorders open November 27 at 22,000 yen per pair.

items.title: SoundPEATS Air6 Pro brings 58dB adaptive ANC and LDAC to its Air line
items.summary: SoundPEATS has released the Air6 Pro earbuds with adaptive hybrid ANC rated up to 58 dB, an 11 mm driver and Bluetooth 6.0 on the Qualcomm QCC3091 chip. The buds support LDAC, aptX Lossless, Snapdragon Sound, Dolby Audio and LE Audio, with up to 12 hours per charge and 52 hours with the case. Black Friday pricing has already taken over at 71.99 dollars with an on-page coupon.

items.title: Cleer Bridge open-ear clip-on earbuds launch with Red Dot award, Dolby Audio
items.summary: Cleer Audio launched Cleer Bridge, open-ear clip-on true wireless earbuds priced at 159.99 dollars, on November 23. A 2026 Red Dot Best of the Best winner, the buds pair a 12 mm titanium driver with Dolby Audio, Snapdragon Sound, aptX Lossless and Hi-Res Wireless certification. Cleer rates battery life at 7 hours per charge and 23 hours with the case, with an IPX5 build.

items.title: Honor Earbuds Clip: 5.6-gram open-ear buds launch at 449 yuan
items.summary: Honor introduced the Earbuds Clip open-ear clip-on earbuds alongside the Honor 700 series on November 23, with sales starting November 27 at 449 yuan. Each bud weighs 5.6 grams and uses a food-grade liquid silicone C-bridge with titanium memory metal, a 10.8 mm titanium-plated driver and LHDC 5.0 lossless audio. Honor rates battery life at 10 hours per charge and 40 hours with the case, with an IP54 rating.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro fall to their lowest price yet
items.summary: The Galaxy Buds 4 Pro dropped to 179.99 dollars on Amazon on November 20, a 70 dollar or 28 percent discount off the 249.99 dollar list price. The flagship true wireless earbuds feature a two-way speaker setup, adaptive ANC, Live Translation, Seamless Codec and spatial audio with head tracking. Battery life is rated at 6 hours with ANC on and up to 26 hours with the case.

items.title: Xiaomi's unusual open-ear earbuds make their way to Europe
items.summary: Xiaomi has brought its Clip clip-on open-ear earbuds to Europe from 149.99 euros, after a Chinese debut in May and a global introduction on November 17. The buds use 11 mm drivers, Bluetooth 5.4 and LHDC 5.0, weigh 5.5 grams each and carry an IP57 rating. Xiaomi advertises 38 hours of playback with the case in AAC, dropping to 25 hours with LHDC 5.0 enabled.

items.title: Xiaomi Clip could be the best clip-on open earbuds tested so far
items.summary: TechRadar published hands-on impressions of the Xiaomi Clip on November 17 after two weeks of testing, calling them potentially the best open earbuds the reviewer has tried. The first cuff-style open-ears from Xiaomi use an 11 mm driver with a V-shaped sound signature, a tiny charging case and sound leakage reduction. A UK price of 129 pounds and a European price of 149.90 euros were confirmed, but the US price remains unconfirmed.

items.title: Five TWS earbuds under 2,000 rupees compared for value
items.summary: Hindustan Times compared five budget true wireless earbuds under 2,000 rupees on November 10, covering models from OnePlus, boAt, realme, Noise and Skullcandy. The roundup weighs battery claims, active noise cancellation, low-latency modes and dual-device connectivity against real customer feedback. It notes that cheaper models often force trade-offs between playback time, call quality and reliability.

items.title: Open wireless stereo defies falling global audio market, Omdia says
items.summary: Omdia data reported on October 3 shows global true wireless stereo shipments fell 0.7 percent year on year to 82.1 million units in the second quarter of 2026, the first annual decline since 2023. Open wireless stereo shipments grew 12 percent to 11.1 million units, reaching 13.5 percent of total TWS volume, with clip-on designs taking 61 percent. Omdia forecasts open wireless shipments rising from 43.9 million units in 2026 to 90.5 million by 2030.
